hook: A bacterial enzyme activates oxygen using ferric iron, unlike most oxygen-using enzymes.
summary: A crystal structure of OzmD, plus EPR and Mossbauer spectroscopy of a close homologue, show the iron starts as Fe(III) and is reduced by the substrate before it activates oxygen. OzmD also acts as a dioxygenase on a substrate analog, tying bacterial and fungal DUF4243 enzymes. Full mechanisms are proposed from precedent and computation, not directly observed.
title: Decyanation, Dioxygenation, and Oxidative Ring Contraction Catalyzed by the DUF4243 Oxidase OzmD Rely on Ferric Oxygen Activation
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
